brief: 6 pricing moves that quietly compounded my revenue while I stopped discounting.

slots.subtitle: Six quiet moves that reshaped my revenue and made every sale more profitable than the last.
slots.preview1: How I raised prices without losing customers
slots.preview2: The bundling trick that doubled average order value
slots.preview3: Why anchoring beat every sale I ever ran

slots.title: Set the
slots.subtitle: The first price a customer sees sets the mental ceiling for everything below it.
slots.insight1Body: Show your most expensive tier before any other option on the page.
slots.insight2Body: Insert a middle tier that makes the target plan feel like a steal.
slots.insight3Body: Discounting from a low base destroys your margin forever.
slots.pullQuote: If you lead with cheap, you spend forever proving you're worth more.

slots.title: Bundle for
slots.subtitle: Packaging features together changed how customers perceived my product's total worth.
slots.insight1Body: Combine three tools into one SKU that feels like a complete solution.
slots.insight2Body: Call the bundle 'Studio' or 'Pro Suite' to signal professional grade.
slots.insight3Body: Remove individual pricing so the bundle becomes the obvious choice.
slots.pullQuote: Bundles don't just raise ticket size; they erase comparison shopping entirely.

slots.title: Collect cash
slots.subtitle: Upfront annual plans injected immediate cash and cut my monthly cancellation risk.
slots.insight1Body: Frame the annual discount as 'twelve months for the price of ten'.
slots.insight2Body: Show the annual toggle first; monthly becomes the downgrade option.
slots.insight3Body: Guarantee the price for twenty-four months to remove renewal friction.
slots.pullQuote: Cash today is worth more than promises of cash tomorrow.

slots.title: Price by
slots.subtitle: I stopped billing for seats and started pricing against the revenue my tool generated.
slots.insight1Body: Set fees as a fraction of the value your customer actually captures.
slots.insight2Body: Per-user pricing caps your growth inside their headcount budget.
slots.insight3Body: Scale the price only when the customer's metric scales upward.
slots.pullQuote: When you price for outcomes, discounts become mathematically unnecessary.

slots.title: Kill the
slots.subtitle: Eliminating my freemium plan forced serious buyers to commit and raised support quality.
slots.insight1Body: A seven-dollar seven-day trial converts higher than a bloated free tier.
slots.insight2Body: Paywalls filter out users who were never going to convert anyway.
slots.insight3Body: If the product costs something, people actually show up to use it.
slots.pullQuote: Free users scale your costs; paid trials scale your conviction.

slots.title: Lift the
slots.subtitle: I finally increased legacy rates and discovered most customers never even flinched.
slots.insight1Body: Give sixty days notice so the increase feels fair, not predatory.
slots.insight2Body: Let existing users keep the old rate for one extra renewal cycle.
slots.insight3Body: Ship one new feature the week before the new pricing takes effect.
slots.pullQuote: The customers who threaten to leave over ten dollars were already leaving.

slots.ctaBody: Six pricing moves that replaced discounting with real, compounding revenue. Your margin is your mission.
